# Public sector and regulated security

Applies when the change touches: government or audited systems. Every role loads this pack for the steps it works in, on top of its own playbook. The test commands below are best practices the gate runs: put them in the Spec's `[[tests.commands]]`, so a red one blocks the merge. Name the pack in the Spec's Context; it does not count against a Task's `skills`.

## Standards

| Standard | Edition | Checked | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NIST CSF | 2.0 (published 2024-02-26); NIST CSWP 29 | 2026-09-28 | <https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/cswp/29/the-nist-cybersecurity-framework-csf-20/final> |
| NIST SP 800-53 | Rev. 5, Release 5.2.0 (published 2025-08-27) | 2026-09-28 | <https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final> |
| FedRAMP Rev. 5 baselines, where they apply | Rev. 5; Rev. 5 is on fedramp.gov's legacy pages, for reference during the transition to the Consolidated Rules for 2026 (FedRAMP 20x); FedRAMP stops accepting new Rev. 5 certifications on 2027-06-11 | 2026-09-28 | <https://www.fedramp.gov/legacy/> |
| FedRAMP 20x (emerging) | Consolidated Rules for 2026: Classes A, B, and C final; Class D (High) in Phase 4; the current FedRAMP program (Phase 3, wide-scale adoption, through FY26 Q4); Rev. 5 stays for existing certifications until its transition path is set | 2026-09-28 | <https://www.fedramp.gov/20x/> |
| FIPS 140-3 cryptography | FIPS 140-3 (published 2019-03-22) | 2026-09-28 | <https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/140-3/final> |
| NIST post-quantum standards (FIPS 203, 204, 205) for new cryptography | FIPS 203, FIPS 204, FIPS 205 (published 2024-08-13) | 2026-09-28 | <https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/203/final> |
| NIST Privacy Framework where a US privacy-programme mapping is needed | Version 1.0 (2020); Version 1.1 at Initial Public Draft as of 2026-09 | 2026-09-28 | <https://www.nist.gov/privacy-framework> |

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item |
| --- | --- |
| Entry (`aidd next`) | Government or audited systems: the compliance dimension, major, evidence retained for the audit. |
| Specify | Map the change to the NIST SP 800-53 controls it touches; FIPS-validated cryptography named for any crypto change. |
| Implement | Logging and audit trails per the control baseline; no new cryptography outside the validated modules. |
| Review | Control mapping and evidence complete; the POA&M updated for any accepted risk. |
| Ship | Continuous-monitoring signals watched; the change record retained with the gate record. |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Control mapping | the touched controls are named and reviewed | OSCAL or the team's control matrix |
| SAST, dependency, and container scanning | no high finding | Semgrep or CodeQL; OSV-Scanner; Trivy |
| Cryptography inventory | only FIPS 140-3 validated modules | a dependency and configuration check |
| Audit log tests | every privileged action is logged with actor, time, and outcome | integration tests |
| Accessibility check | user-facing changes meet Section 508 and WCAG 2.2 AA | axe-core or an equivalent |

## Keep it current

A standard marked emerging is a draft, a first edition, or a young practice: apply it only when the change clearly needs it, and say so in the Spec. A standard checked more than a year ago is stale: `aidd eval standards` lists it, and the loop contract's research-first rule applies. When the change needs a standard this pack lacks, look up the authoritative source, record the edition in the Spec's Context, and propose the update to the aidd project's roles registry (`schemas/roles.json` in the aidd repository) as an improvement.
